children: eased Thursday morning to about 4.95%, down seven basis points, after a week that pushed the benchmark through a level last seen on a closing basis in 2007.

Crossing a major psychological yield threshold has often lined up with near-term choppiness in the S&P 500. Seven of the eight such breaks since 1962 arrived in midterm election years—another coincidence this cycle.

Data provided by Bespoke Investment Group shows that when the 10-year has traded with a 5-handle, forward equity results have ranked among the weakest of any yield range: average three-month S&P 500 gains of just 0.4% (positive 56% of the time), six-month gains of 1.3% (57% positive), and one-year gains of 4.1% (64% positive). Those figures sit well below the long-run averages of 2.2%, 4.4%, and 9.1%.

Higher yields can coexist with rising stocks if earnings and liquidity absorb the move. Still, the 5% handle has historically marked a period of thinner equity risk premia and more frequent pauses rather than the strongest stretch of the cycle.
Thursday’s modest pullback keeps the yield just below the line; whether it holds above 5% on a sustained close will decide how relevant that weaker historical cohort remains.

title: History says a 5% US10Y has shown some of the weakest S&P 500 follow-throughs
